title: Aincrad v0.6 developer-only long ecology diagnostic
interpretation: Approximate game ecology with no human agents. The finite energy budget is conserved; the default populations are not balanced. This is one deterministic functional diagnostic, not an ecological or biological validation study.

conditions.weather: Actual seeded weather, advanced once per shared simulation step; no hour or weather overrides.
conditions.plants: Default mature apple trees, brambles and aggregate grass patches.
conditions.animals: Default initialized rabbits, bobcats and foxes; no extra spawn, restock or relocation.
conditions.traceSampling: One sample per surviving animal every 60 simulation seconds; latest 32 samples retained before each death.
conditions.coldExposure: Species fur adjustment in the game engine; no independently validated thermoregulation.

losses.interpretation: Attribution uses actual fatal contact or engine damage thresholds at death; the engine does not emit a separate clinical cause-of-death diagnosis.

limitations: This default map does not sustain every species across the two-week window.
Animal controllers use local reactive movement and steering, not a global route planner.
Severe water deficits preceded both bobcat losses. Navigation or habitat accessibility is a plausible contributor and is supported by the saved movement traces; it was not isolated experimentally.
Initial predator reserve replenishment produces substantial first-day predation.
Reproduction and juvenile bodies are approximations; nursing and detailed developmental physiology are not modeled.
Seasonal resources and local carrying capacity need further calibration before claiming long-term population equilibrium.
